rules.title: Berkeley ban on the sale or use of coordinated pricing algorithms to set rents or manage occupancy (BMC ch. 13.63)
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to sell, license or otherwise provide to Berkeley landlords any coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in Berkeley (§ 13.63.030(A)). It is also unlawful for a landlord to use such an algorithm when setting rents or occupancy levels for Berkeley units (§ 13.63.030(B)). A coordinated pricing algorithm is any analytical or computation process that uses Competitor Data to calculate and recommend rent prices, fees, occupancy rates or other rental contract terms for future leases in coordination between a Berkeley landlord and its competitors, including through a third-party vendor. Competitor Data is non-public information about another owner's or manager's property (actual rents, occupancy rates, lease start and end dates and similar data) that is less than 90 days old. Each month a violation continues, and each unit for which the algorithm was used, is a separate violation. Remedies: the City Attorney may sue under subsections A and B for damages, injunctive relief, restitution of illegal profits and civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation. An aggrieved tenant may sue under subsection B for injunctive relief, money damages and civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation. The prevailing City Attorney or tenant must be awarded attorney's fees and costs, and a lease clause limiting a tenant's fee recovery is unenforceable. The chapter does not regulate the amount of rent and does not bar software that helps landlords manage units generally or through public data.
rules.key_value: Civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation; each month and each unit is a separate violation; mandatory attorney's fees to a prevailing City Attorney or tenant; Competitor Data = non-public data less than 90 days old

coverage.summary: Applies to all residential dwelling units in Berkeley. It covers landlords who use coordinated pricing algorithms and vendors who sell, license or provide them to Berkeley landlords. No unit-count, building-age or landlord-size limits are stated. It operates alongside the state Cartwright Act ban on common pricing algorithms (Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729).
coverage.other_conditions: Excluded products: (a) aggregated, anonymous rental data reports that make no recommendations; (b) products for setting rent or income limits under affordable-housing guidelines; (c) information used for market research for project financing, appraisals, or research, testing or training for software development, provided Competitor Data is not an input when a recommendation is calculated.

rules.exemptions: Excluded from the definition: aggregated and anonymous rental data reports that make no recommendations; products that set affordable-housing rent or income limits; and market research for project financing, appraisals, or software research, testing or training (§ 13.63.020(A)).
rules.effective_date_note: The captured ordinance text (Ord. 7,992-N.S.) has no effective-date clause and no final adoption date. The secondary law-firm alert (DX06, August 21, 2026) lists the chapter as 'effective January 2026'. Status in_force rests on the query date (2026-10-01) falling after any of these dates.

rules.title: Berkeley tenant screening fee disclosure and ban on non-refundable fees for existing tenancies (BMC ch. 13.78)
rules.requirement: An owner or agent who charges a Berkeley applicant a fee to buy a consumer credit report and to process an application must give a clear and conspicuous Tenant Screening Fee Rights Statement and a statement of the maximum fee cap under Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6(b). The disclosure goes either in the rental application or in a separate disclosure before the fee is received (§ 13.78.010). An owner or agent may not charge any existing tenant a non-refundable fee to renew a tenancy, in whole or in part. This includes fees tied to a roommate's departure or to a request to add or replace a roommate (§ 13.78.016). Chapter 13.78 applies to all residential rental agreements regardless of contrary lease language, and lease provisions that violate it are unenforceable (§ 13.78.018).
rules.key_value: Rights statement and fee-cap disclosure required before the fee is received; no non-refundable renewal or roommate fees for existing tenants. The dollar cap itself is state law (the Rent Board lists $68.96 for 2026).

rules.title: Berkeley Rent Ordinance Annual General Adjustment (AGA) limit on rent increases, including the Measure BB 5% cap and the 2026 AGA
rules.requirement:
For fully covered units, the rent ceiling may rise each year only by the Annual General Adjustment (AGA). The Rent Board sets the AGA by a formula tying it to the Consumer Price Index: 65% of the Bay Area CPI-U increase, approved by voters in November 2004 (BMC § 13.76.110A). Measure BB (November 2024) caps the AGA at 5%, even if the formula yields more. A landlord with banked (unused) AGAs from earlier years may still raise rent by more than 5% to reach the rent ceiling. The 2026 AGA (Rent Board Regulation 1148, adopted October 16, 2025) is 1.0%, which is 65% of the 1.5% CPI increase for July 1, 2024 to June 30, 2025. It may be applied to 2025 permanent rent ceilings no earlier than January 1, 2026. It may not adjust rents for tenancies that began on or after January 1, 2025 whose rents were set under the Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act. Regulation 1148 sets the conditions for qualifying and the notice required to tenants. Under Measure BB:
- Fully covered government-owned or -subsidized units now have rent ceilings limited by the AGA.
- Owners may petition for rent increases only for completed capital improvements, not planned ones.
- For tenancies starting on or after February 6, 2024, utilities in fully covered units must be included in base rent or separately metered in the tenant's name.
rules.key_value: 2026 AGA 1.0% (65% of 1.5% CPI), usable no earlier than Jan. 1, 2026; AGA capped at 5% (Measure BB); banked AGAs may exceed 5% up to the rent ceiling

rules.title: Berkeley Rent Ordinance just cause for eviction, notice requirements and owner move-in relocation assistance
rules.requirement:
Tenants in units fully or partially covered by the Rent Ordinance cannot be evicted without just cause (formerly 'good cause').

Measure BB changes to the causes:
- Eviction for nonpayment requires rental debt of at least one month of HUD Fair Market Rent for an equivalent unit (Oakland-Fremont HUD Metro FMR for the fiscal year of the demand).
- A tenant may not be evicted for failing to sign a substantially similar lease when a fixed-term lease expires.
- Lease-breach evictions require a mutually agreed material term, substantial actual damage to the landlord and unreasonable tenant behavior. The prior notice to cease must specify the term and describe the violation and harm.

Notices and filings:
- Every termination notice must state that advice is available from the Rent Board and give the Board's housing counseling phone number and website.
- Copies of termination notices, notices to quit and summons and complaints must be filed with the Rent Board within three business days of service.
- For tenancies starting on or after December 20, 2024, landlords must give a written Notice of Tenant Rights within 15 days of the start of the tenancy and post it in any interior common area.

Owner move-in relocation:
- Owners must pay relocation assistance to tenants evicted for owner move-in.
- Amounts are indexed to inflation and adjusted yearly, which Measure BB made mandatory.
- From January 1, 2026: standard payment $19,413; additional payment for qualifying households $6,471. This is a 1.5% CPI-U (SF-Oakland-San Jose) adjustment approved by the Rent Board on October 16, 2025.
rules.key_value: Nonpayment eviction only if debt is at least 1 month of HUD FMR; filings with the Rent Board within 3 business days; tenant rights notice within 15 days (tenancies from Dec. 20, 2024); owner move-in relocation $19,413 standard + $6,471 for qualifying households (from Jan. 1, 2026)

rules.title: Berkeley Ellis Implementation Ordinance relocation assistance
rules.requirement: When an owner evicts tenants in order to remove a property from the rental housing market (Ellis Act withdrawal), the owner must pay the same relocation assistance as for an owner move-in eviction. The payments are indexed to inflation, and the Rent Board publishes the yearly increase. From January 1, 2026, the standard payment is $19,413 and the additional payment for qualifying households is $6,471. This is a 1.5% CPI-U (SF-Oakland-San Jose) adjustment approved by the Rent Board on October 16, 2025.

rules.title: Berkeley Rent Ordinance security deposit interest requirement
rules.requirement: For tenancies in units fully or partially covered by the Rent Ordinance, landlords must pay tenants interest on the security deposit at the end of each year. If the tenant moves out before year-end, the landlord must pay a prorated amount. The rate is published on the Rent Board's Security Deposit Interest & Calculator page.
